papers.title: EEG2MCU: Sensing-to-Execution Co-Design for Wearable EEG Inference
papers.summary: Presents EEG2MCU, a sensing-to-execution co-design framework for wearable EEG inference that treats electrode count as a hardware design variable via task-aware montage selection and generates only the INT8 regions needed per first-layer tile. On a Cortex-M7 MCU it reduces peak SRAM by 11.38x (including 1.71x from a 62-to-19 electrode montage), latency by 2.57x, and energy by 2.48x while retaining 94-96% of full-montage accuracy.

papers.title: LogicSleep: a neurosymbolic-guided framework for explainable and personalized sleep staging.
papers.summary: LogicSleep is a neurosymbolic framework combining a CNN-graph U-Net backbone with Conditional Random Fields and differentiable-logic transition rules to produce physiologically valid, subject-adaptive sleep staging. It outperformed strong baselines on ISRUC_S1, ISRUC_S3, and MASS_SS3, including under cross-dataset settings, and improved sequence-level metrics and explainability.

papers.title: Reference Coordinates, Output Perturbations, and Information Loss in EEG Decoding
papers.summary: This work uses measurement-operator theory to distinguish EEG reference-coordinate sensitivity, output perturbation, and electrode-loss effects across three motor-imagery datasets and four decoders. Measurement-operator canonicalization (MOC) reduced reference disagreement and improved balanced accuracy versus raw processing at 10 dB output perturbation, though no additional benefit over fixed graph smoothing after pseudoinversion was established, and accuracy alongside consistency was required to assess utility.

papers.title: Exploratory evaluation of electroencephalogram-derived features for classification of mild cognitive impairment in two independent datasets.
papers.summary: This exploratory study evaluated EEG-derived spectral, synchronization-likelihood, and graph-metric features for classifying mild cognitive impairment versus healthy controls in Japanese and Iranian datasets. Lower-alpha-band exponentially transformed features achieved nested cross-validated accuracies of 88.24% (Japanese) and 83.61% (Iranian), but bidirectional cross-dataset transfer dropped to 40.98% and 58.82%, indicating dataset-specific characteristics.

papers.title: Longitudinal resting-state EEG-based modeling predicts phenoconversion and delineates heterogeneity in isolated REM sleep behavior disorder.
papers.summary: Subtype and Stage Inference (SuStaIn) was applied to longitudinal resting-state EEG from 285 participants to model heterogeneity and predict phenoconversion in isolated REM sleep behavior disorder. A progressive degenerative subtype showed delta/theta increases and stage advancement, and subtype shifting or accelerated stage progression identified individuals with exceptionally high phenoconversion risk (survival 0–15% by 7.5 years).

papers.title: Small or large patches? History, biophysics, and an empirical test of a core assumption in EEG independent component analysis
papers.summary: Contrasts the small-patch and large-patch models of EEG independent component dipole interpretation using simulations and resting-state EEG from 820 recordings (14,578 brain ICs). Found 77.6% of fitted dipoles lay >5 mm inward from the template boundary, dipole orientations showed no tangential dominance among deep ICs, and results favored the large-patch model, attributing fitted dipole depths to source spatial extent.

papers.title: Spectral and complexity-based signatures of advanced concentration absorption meditation: A high-density EEG study of jhana
papers.summary: High-density EEG with spectral and complexity measures was used to characterize eight progressively deepening jhana absorption meditation states in 20 advanced meditators alongside phenomenological ratings. The states showed widespread posterior-central power reductions, posterior aperiodic flattening, and elevated entropy-based complexity that persisted into the most minimal states, dissociating neural complexity from experiential richness.

papers.title: Effects of pharmacotherapy on quantitative electroencephalogram measures of sleepiness in obstructive sleep apnea.
papers.summary: Secondary analysis of a randomized trial in 16 OSA participants testing reboxetine alone and with oxybutynin found no significant treatment effect on wake qEEG markers of next-day sleepiness (delta/theta power, theta/alpha ratio) during morning Karolinska Drowsiness Tests, supporting the agents' safety regarding daytime sleepiness. Morning delta and theta power were higher than evening, with frontal predominance, and qEEG did not correlate with subjective sleepiness.

papers.title: Aberrant Interregional Brain Connectivity During Different Memory Processes in a Mouse Model of Alzheimer's Disease.
papers.summary: Using a novel Y-maze paradigm with aversive feedback and local field potential recordings, the study compared memory-related electrophysiology between Alzheimer's model and normal mice, finding widespread oscillatory and directional connectivity disruptions during memory processes that correlated with spatial memory failures. Causal connectivity analyses indicated a disrupted functional balance between cingulate gyrus and hippocampus in AD mice, proposed as early network compensation.

papers.title: Comparison of Infradian and Circadian Rhythms in Laboratory Rodents.
papers.journal: Journal of experimental zoology. Part A, Ecological and integrative physiology
papers.summary: Monitored locomotor activity in CD-1 mice, Mongolian gerbils, and white-tailed antelope squirrels and applied Lomb-Scargle spectral analysis to quantify circadian and infradian rhythms. Circadian rhythms were robust in all animals, whereas infradian (5- and 10-day) rhythmicity was extremely low in mice and moderate in gerbils and squirrels, with strength under 10% of circadian rhythmicity.

papers.title: A mathematical programming approach for the robust resolution of superpositions of action potentials.
papers.journal: Computer methods and programs in biomedicine
papers.summary: The authors formulated action potential superposition resolution as a quadratic mixed-integer programming problem and validated the framework on simulated and experimental intramuscular EMG and neural signals. It resolved superpositions of up to 15 action potentials with over 97% accuracy, handled repeated discharges of the same action potential at 95% accuracy, and maintained 94.6% identification with 32-channel recordings when 80% of action potentials were unknown.

papers.title: Children become accurate years before they become fast: electroencephalography dates the separate maturation of decision components
papers.summary: Analyzing EEG from 1,534 participants aged 5-21 during a contrast-change discrimination task, the study dissociated developmental components of perceptual decisions: accuracy improved via fewer attention lapses and more efficient evidence accumulation reaching half their change by about 9 years, whereas non-decision time shortened only between 11 and 14 years. Visual response strength did not grow with age, indicating accuracy and speed mature on separate timetables.

papers.title: Cross-modality Knowledge Transfer Between fMRI and EEG for Improved Single-modality Alzheimer's Disease Diagnosis.
papers.summary: Proposes FE-KTNet, an fMRI-EEG knowledge transfer network that learns fused multi-scale spatiotemporal representations from paired data and distills them back to modality-specific models through cross-modality fusion and feature/logit alignment. Across 14 multicenter datasets (2,766 fMRI, 1,842 EEG subjects), it improved fMRI-only and EEG-only accuracy by 3.4%/6.1% for AD-NC, 5.2%/8.0% for MCI-NC, and 3.5%/7.1% for AD-MCI versus baselines.

papers.title: Shared-Encoder Residual Task-Bridging Network for Motor Execution to Motor Imagery EEG Transfer in Brain-Computer Interfaces
papers.summary: The authors propose SE-RTBNet, a shared-encoder residual task-bridge network with performance-aware routing for intra-subject cross-task transfer from motor execution to motor imagery EEG decoding. On three public datasets it achieved average classification accuracies of 69.39%, 74.61%, and 98.94%, outperforming existing transfer-learning algorithms and reducing reliance on MI calibration data.

papers.title: A multimodal dataset for the study of cybersickness under stress and mental workload during immersive VR driving.
papers.summary: Presents a multimodal dataset from 60 participants performing phase-based immersive VR driving tasks, with a final phase designed to elicit mental workload, stress, or both. Records EEG, cardiovascular, respiration, and head-movement data alongside self-report cybersickness, workload, and stress measures, and demonstrates changes in cybersickness symptoms across driving phases and conditions.

papers.title: Evidence for decoder-label-regime-dependent effects of complementary leaky integrate-and-fire temporal-state decoding in motor-imagery EEG.
papers.summary: Using identical frozen ATCNet/FBCNet representations compared across BCI2a, OpenBMI, BCI2b, and BNCI2015-001, this work demonstrates a reproducible decoder-label-regime effect in which CLIF-family temporal-state decoders outperform ANN-SEW by 10.082 pp (BCI2a) and 5.470 pp (OpenBMI) under cross-entropy-only training, with attenuation as labels increase (-2.319 pp per label doubling in BNCI2015-001). Hard binary spikes were not necessary, and matched whole-sequence readout reduced CLIF-versus-continuous-decoder differences.

papers.title: Cognitive capacity in subjective cognitive decline: Insights from electrophysiological markers and dual-task performance.
papers.summary: Compared older adults with and without subjective cognitive decline during single and dual working memory/finger-tapping tasks, finding reduced P2 and P3b amplitudes in dual-task conditions and higher theta and alpha power plus slower tapping in the SCD group. Suggests compensatory neural mechanisms and electrophysiological markers that may precede objective cognitive deficits.

papers.title: Cerebellar structural and electrophysiological alterations associated with neuropathic pain in mice.
papers.summary: In mice with sciatic nerve chronic constriction injury, found persistent mechanical hypersensitivity accompanied by cerebellar volumetric changes, reduced absolute delta/theta LFP power in lobules IV-V, and increased multi-unit firing rates and evoked responses. Interprets these as a candidate low-synchrony/high-gain cerebellar operating regime in neuropathic pain.

papers.title: Corticomuscular or electroencephalography-electromyography coherence and intermuscular or electromyography-electromyography coherence.
papers.summary: Reviews the principles and computation of coherence analysis for motor control, covering corticomuscular coherence between EEG/MEG and EMG and intermuscular coherence between EMG signals. Discusses their characteristics and clinical significance in healthy and neurologic conditions.

papers.title: Prolong Life with Nine Turn-Method versus CBT-I for Sleep-Onset Chronic Insomnia: A Randomized Controlled Trial Protocol Integrating fMRI and PSG.
papers.summary: Describes a randomized controlled trial protocol comparing 12-week Prolong Life with Nine Turn-Method versus CBT-I in 128 patients with sleep-onset chronic insomnia, with PSQI change as the primary endpoint. Integrates PSG, resting-state fMRI, EEG network measures, actigraphy, and biomarkers to assess long-term efficacy and cortical network modulation.

papers.title: Neural Profiles of Pistol Shooting Performance Across Skill Levels in Hearing and Deaf Shooters: Insights into Cognitive-Motor Processes.
papers.journal: Medicine and science in sports and exercise
papers.summary: Examined EEG oscillations during the 4 s preceding trigger pull in skilled versus novice hearing (Study 1) and deaf (Study 2) air-pistol shooters. Skilled hearing shooters showed lower temporal alpha asymmetry and higher posterior, frontocentral, and frontal midline theta power, whereas skilled deaf shooters showed reduced frontocentral alpha and sensorimotor rhythm power, indicating expertise-related neural profiles differ with sensory experience.

papers.title: Data-Driven EEG-fMRI Fusion: From Multimodal Integration to Latent Neural Inference.
papers.summary: Reviews data-driven EEG-fMRI fusion methods published 2000-2025, organizing them by symmetric vs. asymmetric strategies, factorization vs. translation objectives, and linear vs. nonlinear assumptions. Reports that fusion reveals distributed network dynamics inaccessible to unimodal analyses, while noting the absence of a universal validation standard and persistent challenges of temporal misalignment and model-dependent interpretation.

papers.title: Brain-computer interfaces in the motor system: The technologies.
papers.summary: Critically reviews brain-computer interface technologies for the motor system, covering noninvasive EEG systems paired with FES feedback for post-stroke rehabilitation and invasive electrocorticography/intracortical arrays enabling robotic control and intracortical-to-FES limb reanimation. Outlines design considerations, decoding and AI approaches, hybrid neural-peripheral systems, and barriers to routine clinical adoption.

papers.title: A Latent Variable Perspective on EEG Measures of Attentional Control
papers.summary: Recorded EEG during four attentional control paradigms (change detection, go/no-go, Simon, Stroop) and tested whether P3 and decoding-accuracy measures load onto a common latent attentional-control factor. Despite robust within-task group-level effects, correlations were weak and structural equation modeling found no evidence for a common latent factor, questioning the construct validity of these EEG indices for individual differences.

papers.title: Adoption of Routine Intraoperative Raw EEG at a Quaternary Pediatric Centre.
papers.summary: A retrospective single-center study of 26,168 pediatric anesthetic records found that routine intraoperative raw EEG use rose from 17.8% to 28.4% of cases between October 2024 and June 2026, with wide provider-level variation (median 18.1%, range 0.9%-79.5%) only weakly explained by case mix.

papers.title: Commercially available multimodal LLMs for EEG-based prognostication after cardiac arrest.
papers.summary: Tested whether two commercial multimodal LLMs (ChatGPT and Claude) could predict neurological outcome directly from single 10-second EEG images in 33 comatose post-cardiac-arrest patients using five prompting strategies. AUC ranged 0.86-0.99 for ChatGPT and 0.74-1.00 for Claude, with both reaching 93.9% accuracy under few-shot prompting, versus 100% for a dedicated deep-learning model on the same cohort.

papers.title: An Integrated Approach for Early In Vitro Sedation Prediction Utilizing hiPSC Neurons and Human Ion Channel Assays.
papers.summary: Screened 14 sedative and 5 non-sedative compounds in hiPSC-derived neurons via multielectrode array and automated patch-clamp across CNS ion channels (KV1.1, KV2.1, KV3.1, KV7.2/7.3, NaV1.2, K2P2.1, GABAA, α4β2 nAChR). Achieved 94% classification accuracy, with sedatives reducing neural firing and network bursting and several interacting with channels within a 30-fold margin of therapeutic plasma concentrations.

papers.title: ALI MEA60: A porous thin-film microelectrode array for air-liquid interface electrophysiology of 3D excitable tissues
papers.summary: Developed and characterized the ALI MEA60, a porous polyimide thin-film microelectrode array with 60 electrodes for air-liquid interface electrophysiology of 3D excitable tissues, compatible with a commercial acquisition system. Across 41 devices it showed median impedance of 56 kOhms and ~5 uV saline RMS noise, stable recording for at least 60 days with ~85% channel persistence, expected pharmacological responses in neural spheroids and cardiac organoids, and cross-tissue compatibility.

papers.title: Electrophysiological correlates of placebo hypoalgesia and nocebo hyperalgesia during the anticipation and delivery of pain
papers.summary: Feasibility study adapting a placebo-nocebo conditioning pain paradigm to EEG in 20 healthy adults, successfully inducing placebo hypoalgesia and nocebo hyperalgesia via verbal instructions, conditioning, and sham TENS. Found increased theta, alpha, and beta power in placebo vs. control during pain delivery and in nocebo vs. control during anticipation and delivery, with gamma-band power increased in nocebo vs. placebo as a function of perceived pain intensity.

papers.title: Females with Epilepsy Show Menstrual Cycle-linked Alterations in Sensory Induced Plasticity.
papers.summary: Tested visual long-term potentiation across menstrual phases (mid-follicular, mid-luteal, perimenstrual) using EEG and thalamocortical generative modeling in 28 females with epilepsy and 25 controls. Controls showed enhanced P2 potentiation in mid-follicular versus perimenstrual phase, whereas epilepsy patients showed greater potentiation in perimenstrual and mid-luteal phases, with modeling indicating loss of inhibitory control and breakthrough excitability.

papers.title: Differential effects of α-synuclein aggregates on the electrophysiology of SNpc vs VTA dopaminergic neurons in acute mouse slices.
papers.summary: Introduced α-synuclein aggregates into single SNpc versus VTA dopaminergic neurons in acute mouse slices and found increased whole-cell conductance and altered firing in SNpc neurons, effects partly reversed by the KATP channel inhibitor glibenclamide. These electrophysiological effects were absent or much weaker in VTA neurons, indicating selective vulnerability mediated in part by KATP channels.

papers.title: Spreading voltage buildup in high density EEG during migraine aura: A longitudinal single-patient study.
papers.summary: Longitudinal 256-channel high-density EEG in a single patient with migraine with aura detected a spreading voltage buildup with contralateral maximum and spreading delta-band power increase during aura, with an estimated spread velocity of 3.8 mm/min, suggested to reflect cortical spreading depolarization.

papers.title: Transcranial magnetic stimulation-electroencephalography - relation to motor physiology.
papers.summary: Reviews how TMS combined with EEG of the motor cortex yields TMS-evoked potentials (P30, N45, P60, N100, P200), detailing their generators and pharmacology and their emerging diagnostic and prognostic utility in motor stroke and Parkinson disease.

papers.title: Report-derived interictal epileptiform discharge burden is associated with 7-day antiseizure medication decisions after pediatric video electroencephalography.
papers.summary: In a retrospective cohort of 216 pediatric video-EEG report episodes, a three-level interictal epileptiform discharge burden abstracted from qualitative report wording was associated with new antiseizure medication initiation within 7 days (adjusted OR 2.89 per higher burden grade; initiation rates 13.0%, 42.9%, 70.0%). Treatment intensification findings in the established-epilepsy cohort were exploratory and non-causal.

papers.title: Clinical use of transcranial magnetic stimulation combined with electroencephalography in the motor system.
papers.summary: Reviews TMS-EEG as a tool to assess cortical inhibition and excitation, oscillatory activity, and effective connectivity in the motor system, summarizing disease-specific network mechanisms and associations with motor impairment, recovery, and treatment response in stroke, ALS, Parkinson disease, and multiple sclerosis.

papers.title: Surgical outcomes in stereoelectroencephalography versus subdural grids: a systematic review & meta-analysis.
papers.summary: Systematic review and meta-analysis of seven studies (1,156 SEEG and 737 subdural grid patients) found higher odds of postoperative seizure freedom with SEEG (OR = 1.72, 95% CI 1.33-2.22), with SEEG also associated with lower infection rates and reduced postoperative analgesic requirements, though the authors caution that compared populations differed clinically.

papers.title: Validation of drug-resistant epilepsy identification algorithms in US Veterans across diverse care settings.
authors: Veterans Epilepsy Learning, Collaborative Research, and Operations (VELCRO) investigators
papers.summary: This multicenter retrospective validation study evaluated 96 medication- and utilization-based algorithms for identifying drug-resistant epilepsy in 970 US Veterans on ≥2 antiseizure medications, using chart review as reference. The best algorithm (3+ ASMs, or 2 ASMs for ≥1 year, plus EEG/MRI and intractable ICD code documentation) achieved AUC 0.701 overall (0.756 CEC, 0.678 non-CEC), supporting standardized DRE identification in VHA administrative data.

papers.title: Influenza A-Associated Encephalitis and Encephalopathy in Adults: An Exploratory Criteria-Based Analysis.
papers.summary: Retrospective exploratory analysis of five adults with PCR-confirmed influenza A and acute neurological symptoms, applying International Encephalitis Consortium 2013 criteria to classify three as encephalitis and two as encephalopathy. The study found the categories overlapped substantially and did not determine treatment, with three patients asymptomatic at 3 months and two with persistent deficits.

papers.title: De novo POLR2A p.(L1127F) variant presenting with neurodevelopmental regression and dystonia, with favorable response to low-dose dopamine therapy: a case report and literature review.
papers.summary: This case report describes a girl with a de novo POLR2A p.(L1127F) variant causing NEDHIB who presented with neonatal hypotonia, later sleep-associated dystonia-like nodding, and neurodevelopmental regression with loss of walking, sitting, and language. Low-dose levodopa-benserazide produced marked motor and cognitive improvement and complete resolution of nodding episodes.

papers.title: Coal Tar-Based Driveway Sealant Extract Induces Mutations in Liver, Bone Marrow, and Germ Cells of MutaMouse Male Mice.
papers.summary: Using Duplex Sequencing, the authors assessed mutagenicity of a coal tar-based driveway sealant extract in MutaMouse male mice and found significant dose-dependent increases in mutation frequency in liver and bone marrow, with spectra dominated by C:G > A:T substitutions resembling a tobacco-smoking-associated mutational signature. Germ cells showed no statistically significant increase by duplex sequencing but a positive dose-response trend, with mutagenicity supported by a significant increase in mutant frequency in the lacZ plaque assay.

topic.label: EEG & Signal Methods
topic.description: EEG signal processing, sleep staging, neural time series, modeling, and practical analysis methods.
